videos.title: Reverse Side Pressure Armwrestling: No, This Isn't a Joke
videos.summary:
Reverse side pressure might sound like a contradiction, but it is one of the most effective weapons in elite arm wrestling, and in this video we break it down properly.

Using a simple prop from our family history, we show exactly what happens to an opponent's hand and wrist alignment the moment you initiate after the go. We walk through the two things you need in place before it can work: winning the centre in the setup, and a locked-in hand built on thumb and palm pronation, deviation and rigid fingers. 

From there, we explain how a deliberate pivot changes the angle of the match, why it breaks the chain at the wrist, and why it leaves your opponent unsure whether they can even commit sideways.

Finally, we show how it fits into a complete game plan, from static side pressure to win centre, to reverse side pressure to break their structure, to leading side pressure to finish the match.

If you compete and want to understand top roll at a deeper level, this one is for you.

videos.title: How to Get Stronger at Armwrestling: What Actually Works
videos.summary:
How do you get stronger at arm wrestling?

It's the most searched question in our sport, and almost everyone answers it wrong. They chase heavier lifts. They try to make weak habits stronger. They run from the grip and call it technique.

Arm wrestling isn't a deadlift. You're not pulling against a bar. You're against another human, and that changes everything. The table is still the best place to get stronger — more than any gym session — if you train the right habits early.

The habit that kills potential is running: backing out of the grip, living on the fingers, hoping to float over the top. You lose side pressure. You lose control. You teach your body the wrong fight.

The habit that raises your ceiling is gripping deep. As high as you can be while still as deep as you can be. Hold on. Take the losses now. Full wrist, full pronation, full side pressure, full back. That's where real arm wrestling strength is built — and it's the only path that holds up when the humans across from you get serious.

Grip deep. Engage the fundamentals. That's how you get strong at this sport.
